Subject: Re: QBR inputs + two clarifications for our execs

Tessa  quick tech note you can pass to Acme: 

- Region pinning + on-prem fallback: Dedicated supports region pinning natively. Automatic on-prem fallback requires the optional bridge (edge appliance) to be deployed; without the bridge fallback is manual. Enabling the bridge is a separate line item on Dedicated orders (typical uplift ~15-20% of committed capacity depending on size).

- Failover modes: We offer (a) automatic failover with health probes (recommended for minimal RTO) and (b) manual controlled failover for customers that require human approval. Automatic mode presumes the bridge has network access to report health and KV synchronization.

- 90-day token retention: Private deployments can export and retain token-level logs, but 90-day persistence is treated as an exception requiring legal sign-off and SOC2 artifact confirmation; operationalizing retention may require additional storage allocation.

Attaching pointer to SOC2 evidence and our ops runbook.

-Aditya
Senior Product Manager, Serving Runtime

Attachments: acme_soc2_evidence.zip (pointer), runtime_ops_runbook.pdf (attachment stub)

For the 90-day token retention exception: procurement will need the SOC2 evidence and a short amendment to the SOW specifying retention scope. Ben (procurement partner) is cc'd and can help with amendment language or an attestation path if Acme is willing to accept that.

Marissa

I've attached the consolidated one-pager and the draft exception matrix. Please let me know if you'd like a short call tomorrow to walk the execs through this.
